prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Miami. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Miami for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but before I give names I need one quick thing: do you mean Miami, FL (Greater Miami / Miami-Dade County)? And what matters most to you: lowest cost, fastest treatment, highest specialty expertise, sedation/surgical comfort, or having work done by one provider (same doctor places and restores the implant) versus referred specialists?

If you want immediate next steps, here’s a practical plan you can use right now (including which specific places to call or how to find them) and why each is useful.

Who to call (specific types of practices and why)
- University dental clinic (University of Miami School of Dental Medicine)
  - Why: faculty-supervised care, lower fees, multi-specialty resources (periodontics, oral surgery, prosthodontics), good if you want a thorough consult or have a tighter budget.
- Oral & maxillofacial surgery practice in Miami
  - Why: best for complex extractions, bone grafting, sinus lifts and medically complex patients. Oral surgeons place implants and handle surgical complications.
- Periodontist with implant specialty
  - Why: specialists in the gums and bone who focus on implant placement and tissue health; often recommended for esthetic zone implants.
- Prosthodontist or restorative dentist experienced in implants
  - Why: prosthodontists design and restore the implant crown/bridge — important for fit, function and esthetics, especially for front teeth or full-mouth cases.
- Multi-specialty implant center (dental implant center / “implant & restorative” centers)
  - Why: coordinated care (placement + restoration) under one roof, often digital workflows (CBCT, guided surgery) and financing options.
- A top-reviewed private dentist in your neighborhood who advertises implant placement and digital imaging
  - Why: convenient and appropriate for straightforward single-tooth implants if they use CBCT and have referrals to specialists when needed.

How to find specific offices quickly
- Use these directories and search terms:
  - AAID “Find an Implant Dentist” and American Academy of Periodontology directories
  - ADA Find-a-Dentist
  - Google Maps / Yelp / Zocdoc: search “dental implants near [zip code or neighborhood],” sort by rating and recent reviews
- Look for clinics that list: CBCT 3D imaging, bone grafting/sinus lift, implant brands (Nobel Biocare, Straumann, Zimmer, Dentsply Sirona), and a prosthodontist on staff or a close restorative partner.

What to ask when you call (short phone script)
- “Do you place dental implants and do you do the restoration here or refer out?”
- “Who places the implant — a periodontist, oral surgeon, or general dentist? How long have they been placing implants?”
- “Do you use 3D CBCT scans and guided implant planning?”
- “Which implant systems/brands do you use?”
- “Do you do bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed?”
- “Estimated total cost range for a single implant (placement + abutment + crown) and whether that includes any scans, grafts or follow-up.”
- “Average timeline from placement to crown, and sedation options.”
- “Can I see before/after photos and patient references or reviews?”

Red flags to avoid on the phone
- No CBCT or no referral path for bone grafts/complicated cases
- No clear treatment plan or vague cost answers
- Pushy hard-sell for immediate “same-day implants” without explanation of case selection

How to compare options
- Get at least 2–3 written estimates with itemized costs (surgery, implant, abutment, crown, grafting, temporary teeth)
- Prefer practices that show credentials (board certification, specialty training) and use CBCT/digital planning
- Consider calling a university clinic if cost is a major concern, and a private specialist if you want fastest/highest-expertise care

If you want, tell me:
- your zip code or neighborhood in Miami,
- whether you prefer the lowest cost vs fastest treatment vs highest specialty,
and I’ll list 4–6 specific clinics (names, general reasons to call each, and what to ask) based on typical, reputable options in the area.
